# F4: thermal imaging, AGC and TI materials {#sec-fg-thermal-agc}

The engine renders thermal imaging from a per-object temperature model. It
does not blit a texture to the screen. A material's `StageTI` texture feeds
that model. This page states the pattern that works, the pattern that fails,
the engine limits, and the defect a wrong value shows.

## What works

A material's `StageTI` block carries four heat-source channels. Red is
solar gain, green is base and active heat, blue is moving parts, and alpha
is metabolism. The BI Community Wiki page "Thermal Imaging Maps" (oldid
155895) states these semantics {src:pbo:Addons/data_f.pbo}. The engine's
own `data_f\default_TI.rvmat` points its `StageTI` at
`a3\data_f\default_ti_ca.paa`, a flat red map with solar gain only
{src:cfg:default_TI.rvmat>>StageTI.texture}.

A surface needs a `class StageTI { texture = ... }` block to render in the
engine thermal mode. A material with a grey diffuse and no `StageTI` does
not render thermal at all {src:adr:ADR-019}.

Per-optic thermal keys describe the sensor. AEE declares `thermalMode[]`,
`thermalNoise[]` and `thermalResolution[]` on the optic class
{src:script:addons/thermal/generated/ThermalOptics.hpp}. The `thermalMode[]`
array names the native palettes, where 0 is WHOT and 1 is BHOT
{src:cfg:CfgWeapons>>ItemInfo>>OpticsModes>>thermalMode}. AEE reads the
array to test whether an optic supports native thermal
{src:script:addons/thermal_display/functions/fusion/fnc_isFusionCapable.sqf}.

A script swaps one material on one named selection. `setObjectMaterial`
takes a selection index and a material path {src:cmd:setObjectMaterial}.
AEE reads the material a model declares from `hiddenSelectionsMaterials`
before the swap {src:script:addons/material/functions/fnc_getObjectMaterial.sqf}.

The display track draws its own thermal palette over the engine day (DTV)
channel. The ppEffect stack applies only when the optic declares a thermal
mode {src:script:addons/thermal_display/functions/display/fnc_applyThermalVision.sqf}.
The sensor lifecycle stays with optics and the render primitives stay with
thermal {src:adr:ADR-006}.

## What does not work

A per-pixel temperature is impossible. The engine simulates one temperature
per object, so a whole surface reads as one value {src:adr:ADR-019}.

A runtime GDT surface mask does not exist. The GDT surface mask is baked
into the WRP, and no command swaps a terrain material at run time
{src:pbo:Addons/data_f.pbo}. Terrain, vegetation and rock stay engine-baked
and are reachable only through the second sun term {src:adr:ADR-019}.

Glass thermal reflection needs a custom model. A stock model does not carry
the `NoTiWrite` render flag on its glass. Only `setObjectMaterial` per
selection reaches the glass, and then only when the model ships
`hiddenSelections` {src:cmd:setObjectMaterial}.

The native thermal pass is out of reach. The renderer is compiled, and a
ppEffect does not apply in the engine vision mode 2 {src:adr:ADR-019}. A mod
therefore cannot put its own palette on the engine thermal channel and must
run its display on the day channel {src:script:addons/thermal_display/functions/display/fnc_applyThermalVision.sqf}.

## Limitations

Three native heat slots exist. `setVehicleTIPars` takes an engine, a wheels
and a weapon value only {src:cmd:setVehicleTIPars}. Beyond the three slots
a surface needs a per-selection material swap
{src:script:addons/thermal/functions/display/fnc_applyEngineThermal.sqf}.

The engine heat is whole-model. The display window can compress and offset
the object temperature curve, and it cannot rebuild the scene
{src:cmd:setTIParameter}.

No terrain material command exists. A PBO path override changes the baked
baseline at load and never at run time {src:pbo:Addons/data_f.pbo}.

The optic palette pair is fixed. The engine config declares no green-hot,
red-hot or ironbow palette, so AEE emits the two-mode WHOT and BHOT pair
{src:script:addons/thermal/generated/ThermalOptics.hpp}.

The AGC window holds on a steady scene. The automatic gain control accepts a
new window only when it moves by more than `_AGC_DEADBAND` of its own span,
and the value is 0.25 at line 340
{src:script:addons/thermal/functions/solver/fnc_updateThermalAGC.sqf}. The
probe P79 measures the window extremes, and the probe P134 covers the
thermal startup path {src:probe:P79}. The hold contract lives in the kernel
test, which pins the value and the window-extreme model
{src:probe:P134}.

## Breaks visually

A hunting AGC window shimmers. A sub-band scene move repaints every
selection when the band is too small, so the settled window must hold
{src:script:tools/tests/test_thermal_optics.py}. The measured floor swing is
5.0 percent of the span, and the window maximum moves about 12.7 percent, so
the band clears both motions {src:probe:P79}.

A wrong selection index paints the wrong part of the model. The index comes
from the `hiddenSelections[]` array and starts at 0
{src:cmd:setObjectMaterial}. An index off by one swaps the material on the
wrong part {src:script:addons/material/functions/fnc_getObjectMaterial.sqf}.

A swapped `StageTI` channel changes the heat reading. A red channel that
should carry solar gain but carries active heat makes a cold object read hot
{src:pbo:Addons/data_f.pbo}. The alpha channel is metabolism, so a swap with
blue removes the barrel heat from a weapon
{src:cfg:default_TI.rvmat>>StageTI.texture}.
